zh: 忙翻了、事情多到做不完
definition: having so much work that you can hardly deal with it
example: I'm completely swamped this week, so can we meet on Monday?
example_zh: 我這週忙翻了，我們可以星期一再約嗎？

zh: 代班、暫時接手（某人的工作）
definition: to do someone's work for them while they are away
example: Could you cover for me at the meeting on Friday?
example_zh: 週五的會議你可以幫我代一下嗎？

definition: a warning or piece of information given in advance
example: Thanks for the heads-up about the office move.
example_zh: 謝謝你先提醒我辦公室要搬家。

definition: to look at or explain something carefully from beginning to end
example: Let's go through the contract together before we sign it.
example_zh: 簽約前我們一起把合約仔細看過一遍吧。

definition: to learn the latest information about something so you can work on it
example: It took me a week to get up to speed on the new project.
example_zh: 我花了一週才進入新專案的狀況。

zh: 把（某人）加進討論、讓某人知情
definition: to include someone in a conversation or email so they know what is happening
example: I'll loop in Jenny so she knows what we decided.
example_zh: 我會把 Jenny 加進來，讓她知道我們的決定。

definition: used to tell someone they do not need to do something quickly
example: Send it whenever you can. No rush.
example_zh: 你方便的時候再寄就好，不急。

definition: used to thank someone and say you will help them in return later
example: Thanks for staying late. I owe you one!
example_zh: 謝謝你留下來加班，欠你一次！

definition: making progress as planned and likely to finish on time
example: The project is on track to launch in March.
example_zh: 專案進度正常，預計三月上線。

definition: an important stage or event in the progress of a project
example: Finishing the beta version was a big milestone for the team.
example_zh: 完成測試版對團隊來說是個重要的里程碑。

definition: to make slower progress than planned
example: If we fall behind this week, we'll have to work on Saturday.
example_zh: 如果這週進度落後，我們週六就得加班。

zh: 阻礙進度的問題、卡關點
definition: a problem that stops work from moving forward until it is solved
example: The missing login details are the main blocker right now.
example_zh: 缺少登入資料是目前最主要的卡關點。

zh: 正式批准、簽核（sign off on something）
definition: to officially approve something so that work can continue
example: Legal signed off on the contract yesterday.
example_zh: 法務昨天簽核了合約。

definition: to finish something, such as a task or a meeting
example: Let's wrap up testing by Friday so we can launch on Monday.
example_zh: 我們週五前把測試收尾，週一就能上線。

zh: 後續追蹤、再跟進（follow up with someone）
definition: to contact someone again to check on something or get more information
example: I'll follow up with the supplier if we don't hear back by Thursday.
example_zh: 如果週四前沒收到回覆，我會再跟供應商追一下。

definition: a person or group with an interest in how a project turns out
example: We send a short update to all stakeholders every Friday.
example_zh: 我們每週五寄一份簡短的進度報告給所有相關單位。

definition: a legal agreement that lets you rent a home for a fixed period
example: My lease ends in March, so I need to decide whether to renew it.
example_zh: 我的租約三月到期，所以要決定要不要續約。

definition: money you pay a landlord before moving in, which you get back if you don't damage anything
example: The security deposit is two months' rent.
example_zh: 押金是兩個月的房租。

definition: services such as electricity, water and gas, or the bills you pay for them
example: The rent is reasonable, but utilities aren't included.
example_zh: 房租還算合理，但不含水電瓦斯。

definition: one problem that is serious enough to make you say no to something
example: Not having a washing machine isn't a deal-breaker for me, but not having an elevator is.
example_zh: 沒有洗衣機我還能接受，但沒有電梯就不行。

definition: something that is much cheaper than you would expect
example: At that price, a two-bedroom near the MRT is a steal.
example_zh: 捷運站附近的兩房只要這個價錢，根本是撿到便宜。

definition: already containing furniture such as a bed, sofa and table
example: I'd prefer a furnished place, so I don't have to buy a bed.
example_zh: 我比較想找附家具的房子，這樣就不用買床。

definition: to pay part of the money for something so that it is kept for you
example: If you like the place, you can put down a deposit today.
example_zh: 如果你喜歡這間，今天就可以先付訂金。

definition: to watch carefully so that you notice something when it appears
example: Can you keep an eye out for apartments near your office?
example_zh: 你可以幫我留意你公司附近的房子嗎？

definition: a small list of the best options, chosen from a longer list, before the final decision
example: We've got three candidates on the shortlist for the job.
example_zh: 這個職缺我們有三位候選人進入最後名單。

definition: the trip you make to get to work and back home every day
example: My commute takes about forty minutes by train.
example_zh: 我搭火車通勤大約要四十分鐘。

zh: 開放式的（沒有隔間的辦公空間）
definition: describing an office with one large shared space instead of separate rooms (Americans also say "open office")
example: Open-plan offices feel bright, but they can be noisy.
example_zh: 開放式辦公室感覺很明亮，但可能會很吵。

zh: 共用座位制（不固定座位）
definition: a system where workers don't have their own desk and use whichever one is free
example: With hot-desking, you have to clear your desk at the end of every day.
example_zh: 採用共用座位制的話，每天下班都要把桌面清空。

definition: to think carefully about the good and bad points of something before deciding
example: Take some time to weigh the pros and cons before you reply.
example_zh: 回覆之前，花點時間好好權衡一下優缺點。

zh: 取捨、權衡（得到一樣就要犧牲另一樣）
definition: a situation where you accept something bad in order to get something good
example: A bigger office means higher rent. That's the trade-off.
example_zh: 辦公室大一點，租金就比較貴，這就是取捨。

definition: agreeing with and supporting a plan or idea
example: Is everyone on board with the new schedule?
example_zh: 大家都同意新的時程嗎？

zh: （把想法）先給某人看看、問問意見
definition: to run something by someone: to tell someone about an idea or plan to get their opinion or approval
example: Let me run this design by the legal team before it goes out.
example_zh: 這份設計發出去之前，我先拿給法務看一下。

definition: to start a meeting, project, or event
example: We're kicking off the new project on Monday morning.
example_zh: 我們週一早上啟動新專案。

definition: a specific piece of work that must be finished and handed over by a certain date
example: The first deliverable is a test version for the support team.
example_zh: 第一個交付成果是給客服團隊用的測試版。

zh: 範圍蔓延（需求越加越多）
definition: the slow growth of a project as people keep adding new requests
example: If we say yes to every new idea, scope creep will kill our timeline.
example_zh: 如果每個新點子都答應，需求越加越多，時程就毀了。

definition: the person who is responsible for something and whom others go to with questions
example: Jun will be the point person for the two new hires.
example_zh: Jun 會是兩位新同事的負責窗口。

definition: a rough number that is close to the real amount but not exact
example: Can you give finance a ballpark figure for the budget?
example_zh: 你可以先給財務一個預算的大概數字嗎？

definition: to gradually increase speed, effort, or ability, often at the start of something new
example: New team members usually need two weeks to ramp up.
example_zh: 新成員通常需要兩週才能上手。

zh: 簡短聯繫一下、對一下進度
definition: to talk briefly with someone to share news or check how things are going
example: Let's touch base on Friday before the meeting.
example_zh: 我們週五開會前先簡短對一下吧。

zh: 待辦事項（會議後要執行的工作）
definition: a task that someone agrees to do after a meeting
example: Let's end the meeting by going over the action items.
example_zh: 我們最後把待辦事項過一遍再散會。

definition: feeling slightly ill
example: I'm a bit under the weather, so I'll join the meeting by video.
example_zh: 我身體有點不舒服，所以會用視訊參加會議。

definition: to have a body temperature that is higher than normal
example: My son has been running a fever since last night.
example_zh: 我兒子從昨晚開始一直發燒。

definition: a sign that you have an illness, such as a cough or a headache
example: Tell the doctor about all your symptoms, even the small ones.
example_zh: 把所有症狀都告訴醫生，就算是小症狀也要說。

definition: a doctor's written order for medicine, or the medicine itself
example: You can pick up your prescription at the pharmacy downstairs.
example_zh: 你可以到樓下的藥局領處方藥。

definition: to stay away from work for a period
example: You should take time off until you feel better.
example_zh: 你應該請假到身體好一點再說。

definition: to become very tired and unable to work well because you have worked too hard
example: If you keep working until midnight, you'll burn out.
example_zh: 如果你一直工作到半夜，會把自己累垮。

definition: a note from a doctor that says you were too sick to work
example: HR needs a doctor's note if you're out for more than three days.
example_zh: 如果請病假超過三天，人資需要診斷證明。

definition: to rest so that you get your energy back
example: Rest up this weekend so you're ready for Monday.
example_zh: 這個週末好好休養，星期一才有精神。
